chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) used to wear the Yemeni caps, the white ones, the quilted ones, and the ones with two ear-covers during battle, and his turban was the 'Sahab', and he had a 'Burnus' which he would wrap himself in.

key_terms.السَّحَابَ: A specific type of turban, literally 'cloud'
key_terms.الْقَلَانِسَ: Caps or skullcaps worn on the head
key_terms.ذَاتَ الْأُذُنَيْنِ: Having two ears (referring to caps with ear covers)

ai.seo_question: What types of headgear and clothing did the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) wear according to Shia hadith sources?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi details the Prophet’s (peace be upon him and his family) diverse headgear, distinguishing between everyday Yemeni and white caps and the specialized 'Dhat al-Uthnayn' (two-ear) cap worn for battle, alongside his distinctive 'Sahab' turban and cloak. In Shia jurisprudence, this hadith serves as a primary textual basis for the permissibility and recommended nature of wearing caps (qalansawa) and turbans, emphasizing the Prophet’s adherence to the customs of his time while maintaining a dignified appearance. The specific mention of the 'Sahab' turban is often cited by scholars to highlight the Prophet’s unique status and the aesthetic dimensions of his sunnah.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> wore Al-Yemeni cap, and the white, and the quilted one, and the one with the two ear-covers during the battle, and his<sup>saww</sup> turban was the fastening one and it had a hood for it to cover by’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from af-Nawfafiy from af-Sakuniy who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that

the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, would wear a white Yemeniy cape and a quilted one with two ears for the war time. His turban was al-Sahab and a hooded cloak which he would wear.’”
